chapter: Guitarists and the Pierron and Brown bands
title: Tuba versus string bass; Chink Martin
summary: Piron's band featured the tuba while Oliver's used string bass, probably for slap rhythm without a piano. Chink Martin carries tuba and bass on the street at 74.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now, one of the things that was interesting to me is that even though Pierron was a dance orchestra, society dance orchestra, they loved to feature the tuba. And I don't remember very many tubas ever seeing a tuba with Oliver's band. It was always a string bass down there. I think it was because they need that slapping rhythm when they didn't have the piano. They needed that.
Most of the old timers say that the tuba was a little bit heavy. I mean, didn't have quite...
Did you ever see Chink Martin, age 74, walking along the street a mile a minute ahead of everybody else with a tuba under one arm and a bass fiddle under the other? That's a sight.
I've heard Chink, of course, play, remember those records that he made for Tulane one time.
Of course, he was at the end of his rope that night. He didn't care much, but he still enjoys his music. I'll click it a minute so we can come back to something else. There we will.
